newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU court rejects main part of UK working hours case.
newsitem.headline: EU court rejects main part of UK working hours case.

text.p: The European Court of Justice on Tuesday rejected the main part of Britain's challenge to a European Union law on working hours and rest periods.
British Prime Minister John Major said on Monday that if his country lost the case, he would insist that the EU treaty be changed to "protect" Britain from such legislation.
"The Court of Justice dismisses, except on one point, the United Kingdom's application for annulment of the working time directive," the court said in a statement accompanying the judgement.
The court removed a sentence in the law which said that the minimum weekly rest period must include a Sunday. Britain was ordered to pay court costs.

Britain had argued that the whole law should be thrown out because it was improperly adopted under health rules, which require support of only a majority of EU countries, instead of under EU rules requiring unanimity.
In the latter case, Britain would have been able to veto the rules, which it argued are gross interference from Brussels.
